questions.prompt: Match each resource hint to what it does.

pairs.right: Do DNS + TCP + TLS to an origin in advance
Fetch a critical current-page resource early
Fetch a likely future-navigation resource at low priority

questions.explanation: preconnect warms a full connection, dns-prefetch just resolves DNS, preload pulls a current-page resource forward, and prefetch prepares a future navigation.

options.text: Fetching a resource the CURRENT page needs, earlier than the browser would discover it
Fetching a page the user will visit next

questions.explanation: preload pulls a critical current-page resource (LCP image, font, critical CSS/JS) forward. prefetch, by contrast, prepares a future navigation.

questions.prompt: A font <link rel="preload"> must include the ____ attribute (fonts are fetched anonymously), or it's wasted.
questions.explanation: Because fonts fetch in anonymous CORS mode, a preload without crossorigin doesn't match the real request and downloads the font twice. Also set the correct `as`.

questions.prompt: Which are correct uses of hints and priorities? Select all that apply.

options.text: preconnect a few critical origins you'll use immediately
preload only genuinely critical, late-discovered resources
Use fetchpriority="high" on the LCP image

questions.explanation: Precise hints help. Marking many resources high flattens the priority order and can delay the real LCP resource — the opposite of the goal.

questions.prompt: What can the Speculation Rules API do that a plain prefetch cannot?

options.text: Prerender an entire likely-next page in the background for near-instant navigation

questions.explanation: Speculation Rules can prerender a whole next page (not just fetch resources), so clicking through is near-instant — with an eagerness setting to balance benefit against wasted work.

questions.prompt: Order the steps that `preconnect` performs ahead of time.
questions.explanation: preconnect completes the full setup — DNS, then TCP, then TLS — so the eventual request to that origin doesn't pay for it.
